DOJ Opens Criminal Probe of California Mail-In Ballots Despite Judge’s Order
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
With just days to go before historic midterm elections, the Trump administration has issued grand jury subpoenas to local election officials in California, seeking unredacted voter records as part of a criminal investigation into the state’s voter rolls. At least one of the subpoenas was delivered after a federal judge rejected the Justice Department’s effort to force California to immediately set aside 20,000 ballots from people it claims are “likely noncitizens.” Such voter fraud is exceedingly rare. The court determined the move would wreak havoc with an election that is already underway, create a chilling effect on election workers and voters, and discount the votes of citizens. The subpoenas order the election officials to testify before a grand jury in a criminal investigation on November 4, the day after the election.
This comes as a report in Wired found the law firm that helped set up Elon Musk’s super PAC has created a new, nationwide so-called election integrity organization aligned with President Trump’s false claims of election fraud. The nonprofit organization is called the Association of State and Local Election Officials. It was established by lawyer Chris Gober, a former director and top lawyer for Musk’s America PAC. Gober is running as a Republican for Texas’s 10th Congressional District, which is home to the massive Terafab chip factory being built by Tesla and SpaceX.

Corporations Spend $737M on Midterm Elections as Super-Rich Give $4.2B to Super PACs
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
A new analysis by Public Citizen finds corporations have spent at least $737 million so far on the 2026 election cycle — a 60% increase from the 2024 election. That compares to less than $13 million spent by corporations on the 2010 midterm elections, before the Supreme Court ruled in Citizens United that political spending is a form of constitutionally protected free speech.
Meanwhile, super PACs have reported receiving $4.2 billion from 515 donors contributing at least $1 million each this year. The record super PAC spending is led by Elon Musk, who’s contributed at least $445 million during this election cycle.

Corporate Power

Trump Returns to South Carolina to Rally GOP Support as Pollsters Declare Senate Race a Toss-Up
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
President Trump made his second trip to South Carolina in two weeks on Thursday as he seeks to salvage support for Republican candidates in deep-red states ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections. Trump won South Carolina by 18 points two years ago, but recent polls show the state’s Senate race is effectively tied, with even Fox News declaring it a “toss-up.” Incumbent Senator Darline Graham had no experience as an elected official when she was appointed to fill the seat left vacant when her brother, the longtime Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, died in July. Graham faces challenger Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician from Charleston who’s campaigning on her medical record. Andrews opposes cuts to Medicaid and supports a public health insurance option, but has opposed Medicare for All. Senator Graham spoke briefly alongside President Trump at a rally in Rock Hill. She described herself as a “conservative Christian” and her opponent as “batshit crazy.” She also had this to say.
Sen. Darline Graham: “I don’t know about you, but I will not allow the liberals and socialists to turn South Carolina blue. You know what? They can just kiss my ass.”
President Trump has reversed his decision to cancel his plans to rally Republican support in Kansas and Iowa over the weekend. On Thursday the White House said Trump would make shorter appearances at a series of “telerallies” but Trump announced on Friday that he would go to the states.

DOJ Ramps Up Criminal Probe of Alaska Senate Candidate Mary Peltola’s Campaign with Subpoenas
Oct 30, 2026
Image Credit: Al Grillo/ZUMA Press Wire
Link copied
The Justice Department has issued subpoenas in response to a New York Times report that found operatives linked to Democratic Alaskan Senate candidate Mary Peltola successfully recruited a second Dan Sullivan to draw votes from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan on the state’s four-person ballot. Peltola has denied a former staffer’s account that she was aware of the effort. It’s not clear which federal law would justify a federal investigation, though President Trump has called for a criminal prosecution of Peltola and her campaign, while Alaska’s Republican governor has ordered a state criminal and civil investigation.

Famine Declared in Yemeni City of Taiz Amid Houthi Siege
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
In Yemen, the governor of Taiz says the city of roughly 1 million people has entered into famine due to a weekslong siege by fighters with the Ansar Allah movement, known as the Houthis. Human Rights Watch said Thursday the siege could amount to the war crime of using starvation as a method of warfare. The famine declaration came as a Saudi airstrike on Taiz killed 13 people. That followed a Houthi attack on Aden’s airport that injured passengers and halted flights. Meanwhile, the Houthis are rejecting claims by the Saudi-led coalition that Saudi air defenses intercepted missiles fired toward Mecca.

Sen. Chris Murphy Calls Trump’s Plans to Renew Attacks on Iran “Insane”
Oct 30, 2026
Image Credit: Middle East Institute
Link copied
Another tanker has been struck while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian forces reportedly deployed a new tactic of strapping explosives to a small boat. It was at least the 35th attack on a ship near the strait since the start of October. It came after Connecticut Democratic Senator Chris Murphy issued a warning over his recent briefing with Pentagon officials on President Trump’s plans to launch intense new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. Murphy spoke with the Middle East Institute.
Sen. Chris Murphy: “You’ve heard a preview that it would be a short-duration plan. I will just say this: Their plan is insane. It won’t — it won’t — it will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law.”

Russian Strike Kills 14 at Crowded Train Station in Ukraine as Another Ship Is Sunk in Black Sea
Oct 30, 2026
Image Credit: Emergency Service of Ukraine
Link copied
In Ukraine, a Russian drone struck a crowded railroad station in the eastern city of Dnipro on Thursday, killing at least 14 people. More Russian attacks killed at least six people elsewhere in Ukraine. The strikes came after sea drones attacked a Greek container ship off the coast of Bulgaria on Wednesday, sinking the vessel. All 15 crew members were evacuated. It’s the latest in a series of drone strikes on civilian ships in the Black Sea blamed on both Ukraine and Russia. On Wednesday, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis called for a global maritime truce during a meeting of the U.N. Security Council.
Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis: “Just yesterday, another commercial cargo vessel, owned by a Greek company, was attacked and sank in the Black Sea. We strongly condemn this attack. Targeted civilian commercial shipping is completely unacceptable. It is yet another reminder for the urgent need for a global maritime truce, ensuring that commercial vessels can navigate safely and freely, even in times of conflict.”

Ukraine Halts Attacks on Russian Refineries at Trump’s Request, as Russian Diesel Heads Toward U.S.
Oct 30, 2026
Image Credit: Greenpeace
Link copied
The Wall Street Journal reports Ukraine’s military has paused its strikes against Russian oil refineries, at President Trump’s request. The unofficial pause is expected to last through the U.S. midterm elections next week. It began last week, after President Trump called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to step down and after Elon Musk temporarily limited Ukraine’s ability to use the Starlink and Starshield internet satellite networks in its aircraft and drones.
Meanwhile, Greenpeace says it’s tracking seven oil tankers carrying an estimated 288,000 tons of Russian diesel toward the U.S. This week, Senator Richard Blumenthal sent letters to shipping companies warning them that delivering Russian diesel to U.S. ports would violate federal law — despite authorization from the Trump administration. “Reverse course while there’s still time,” Senator Blumenthal wrote.

GEO Group Signs 10-Year Contract to Continue Operating Notorious Tacoma ICE Jail
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
In immigration news, the number of ICE jails nationwide has more than doubled since President Trump returned to office, with his administration allocating billions of dollars for the mass detention of tens of thousands of immigrants.
In Washington state, the troubled Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma will continue to operate for another 10 years, after the for-profit prison company GEO Group signed a $1.5 billion contract with the federal government. Advocates have long reported on human rights violations, including sexual violence, as well as numerous deaths at Northwest, where immigrants have repeatedly staged hunger and labor strikes demanding their release.
Meanwhile, in Minnesota, local station KARE 11 reports the Trump administration used taxpayer funds to purchase a shuttered private prison earlier this year in the rural city of Appleton for nearly $496 million to use as an ICE jail. That amount was more than six times the cost of CoreCivic’s initial offer to sell the prison to the state of Minnesota for about $75 million. This follows an unprecedented $45 billion given to ICE to expand its detention capacity as part of Trump’s so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Meanwhile, the ACLU and a coalition of rights groups are suing the Trump administration over its disappearance of immigrants in ICE custody. The policy allows ICE to hide the whereabouts of people in detention, leaving their families and lawyers unable to locate and communicate with them.

Department of Homeland Security

Human Rights
El Salvador Deploys 2,000 Troops to Haiti
Oct 30, 2026
Image Credit: El Salvador Presidency Handout
Link copied
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti in a move human rights advocates say could further destabilize the nation and add to rising violence. Trump has reportedly backed Bukele’s deployment of troops, with Bukele claiming his soldiers only intend to rescue four Salvadoran aviation technicians who’d been kidnapped by gangs in Haiti. Back in El Salvador, Bukele’s so-called state of exception, first declared in 2022, has led to the arbitrary arrest of tens of thousands of people, many wrongfully accused of being gang members and denied due process rights while imprisoned in torturous conditions. Bukele spoke from San Salvador Thursday.
President Nayib Bukele: “I told the gangs in Haiti, 'We wiped out the gangs in El Salvador, and we can do the same to you.' In other words, it was a warning. And our mission isn’t to wipe out the gangs in Haiti, but our mission is to rescue our four members. Now, if they don’t hand them over willingly, well, we’ll rescue them by force.”

Flávio Bolsonaro Declares He’s Brazil’s “Legitimate” Leader After Trump Helps Him Flee to Miami
Oct 30, 2026
Link copied
The New York Times reports President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro could flee Brazil and enter the United States after Bolsonaro’s election loss to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Despite his defeat, Bolsonaro has declared himself the “legitimate” leader of Brazil, claiming — without evidence — the election results were fraudulent. Trump has also falsely claimed Brazil’s election appeared to be “rigged.”
Bolsonaro faces multiple criminal investigations in Brazil, and authorities had requested he surrender his passport when he escaped to Argentina and then Ecuador before landing in Miami Wednesday on a private plane. Trump will likely grant Bolsonaro permanent residency in the U.S., according to U.S. officials who spoke to The New York Times. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former Brazilian far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for orchestrating a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 election to Lula.

El Departamento de Justicia de EE.UU. inicia una investigación penal sobre las papeletas de voto por correo de California pese a la orden de un juez
30 Oct. 2026
Link copied
A solo unos días de las históricas elecciones de mitad de mandato, el Gobierno de Trump ha emitido citaciones judiciales de un gran jurado a funcionarios electorales locales del estado de California, con el fin de obtener registros electorales sin censuras en el marco de una investigación penal sobre los padrones de votantes del estado. Al menos una de las citaciones se entregó después de que un juez federal rechazara el intento del Departamento de Justicia de obligar a California a apartar de inmediato 20.000 papeletas electorales correspondientes a personas que, según el departamento, “probablemente no son ciudadanas” estadounidenses. Este tipo de fraude electoral es extremadamente inusual. El tribunal dictaminó que la medida causaría caos en unas elecciones que ya están en curso, intimidaría tanto al personal electoral como a los votantes y dejaría sin efecto los votos de ciudadanos estadounidenses. Las citaciones ordenan a los funcionarios electorales testificar ante un gran jurado el 4 de noviembre, el día siguiente de las elecciones, como parte de una investigación penal.
Esto se produce al tiempo que un informe de la revista Wired concluyó que el bufete de abogados que contribuyó a establecer el super comité de acción política de Elon Musk ha creado una nueva organización de alcance nacional que se presenta como una entidad dedicada a la “integridad del proceso electoral” y que respalda las afirmaciones falsas de Trump sobre un supuesto fraude en las elecciones presidenciales de 2020. La organización sin fines de lucro, denominada State and Local Election Officials, fue establecida por el abogado Chris Gober, exdirector y abogado principal del comité de acción política de Musk llamado America PAC. Gober se postula como candidato republicano a la Cámara de Representantes de Estados Unidos por el décimo distrito congresual del estado de Texas, en donde se encuentra Terafab, un enorme centro de fabricación de semiconductores que están construyendo Tesla y SpaceX.
Temas:
Derecho al voto
California
Elon Musk
Las corporaciones han gastado 737 millones de dólares en el actual ciclo electoral de EE.UU. al tiempo que los super comités de acción política declaran haber recibido 4.200 millones en donaciones
30 Oct. 2026
Link copied
Un nuevo análisis de la organización Public Citizen revela que las grandes empresas han gastado al menos 737 millones de dólares en lo que va del ciclo electoral de 2026, lo que representa un aumento del 60% con respecto a las elecciones de 2024. La cifra contrasta con los menos de 13 millones de dólares que las corporaciones destinaron a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de 2010, antes de que la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos dictaminara, en el caso “Citizens United contra la Comisión de Elecciones Federales”, que el gasto político es una forma de libertad de expresión protegida por la Constitución.
Mientras tanto, los súper comités de acción política han declarado haber recibido 4.200 millones de dólares de 515 donantes que aportaron al menos un millón de dólares cada uno este año. Elon Musk, quien ha contribuido con al menos 445 millones de dólares durante el actual ciclo electoral, lidera este gasto récord en los súper comités.

Trump regresa a Carolina del Sur para movilizar el apoyo republicano en una contienda para el Senado de EE.UU. que las encuestadores declaran empatada
30 Oct. 2026
Link copied
El presidente Trump realizó el jueves su segundo viaje en dos semanas al estado de Carolina del Sur, en un intento por recuperar el apoyo a los candidatos republicanos en estados que cuentan con una sólida tradición republicana, en vísperas de las elecciones de mitad de mandato que se celebrarán el martes. Hace dos años, Trump ganó en Carolina del Sur por una diferencia de 18 puntos porcentuales, pero encuestas recientes muestran que la contienda de ese estado para un escaño en el Senado de Estados Unidos está prácticamente empatada e incluso el canal Fox News la ha calificado de “impredecible”. La senadora Darline Graham, quien ocupa actualmente el escaño en disputa, no tenía experiencia en cargos públicos cuando fue designada para ocupar el puesto que dejó vacante su hermano, el senador republicano de larga trayectoria Lindsey Graham, fallecido en julio. Graham se enfrenta con la doctora Annie Andrews, una pediatra de la ciudad de Charleston que basa su campaña en su trayectoria profesional en el ámbito de la medicina. Andrews se opone a los recortes al programa público de salud Medicaid, que ofrece cobertura de atención médica a personas de bajos ingresos residentes en Estados Unidos, y apoya la opción de un seguro médico público. Sin embargo, la candidata demócrata se ha opuesto al programa Medicare para Todos, una propuesta que busca ampliar a toda la población estadounidense la disponibilidad del programa público de salud Medicare. La senadora Graham habló brevemente junto a Trump durante un acto de campaña que se llevó a cabo en la ciudad de Rock Hill. Durante su intervención, Graham se definió como una “cristiana conservadora” y calificó a su rival de “loca de m***da”. Estas fueron otras palabras expresadas por Graham durante su discurso.
Senadora Darline Graham: “No sé ustedes, pero yo no voy a permitir que los liberales y los socialistas conviertan a Carolina del Sur en un estado demócrata. ¿Saben qué? ¡Que me besen el c***”.

We speak with Forensic Architecture’s Eyal Weizman about his new book, Ungrounding: The Architecture of Genocide, a meticulous investigation into Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the physical destruction of the territory and its impact on the Palestinian people.
Forensic Architecture was founded in 2010 as an interdisciplinary research group focused on investigating state violence and human rights violations. Since 2023, Forensic Architecture has focused on producing evidence for South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.
Weizman says “ungrounding” is “a kind of destruction that we have not seen anywhere else,” with Israeli bulldozers “terraforming” the landscape to erase all traces of Palestinian life. With thousands of bodies still unrecovered from under destroyed buildings, Israel’s flattening, extraction and reshaping of the rubble in Gaza is a continuation of its crimes, says Weizman.
“Israel is actively and against court order, against the order of the ICJ, destroying the evidence of the genocide that it has perpetrated,” he says.

AMY GOODMAN: Israel is continuing to commit genocide in Gaza long past the so-called ceasefire agreement. That’s according to a new report out this week from the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The report also accuses Israeli forces of committing crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture and rape.
The Israeli Mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a “misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel” and to, quote, “destroy the Jewish state,” unquote.
The United Nations-commissioned experts said Israel was, quote, “continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” unquote. They found Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire. They also found that the so-called Yellow Line, which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, is increasingly encroaching into Gaza and becoming a de facto border.
Well, the organization Forensic Architecture, which has been mapping Israel’s military conduct in Gaza since October 2023, details exactly how Israel has used the Yellow Line to expand its territorial control of Gaza. Here’s a clip from the project titled “A Cartography of Genocide.”
NARRATOR: When the ceasefire came into effect, most of the area Israel had depopulated remained under its control. This constituted 54% of Gaza, marked by the Yellow Line. The Yellow Line is meant to mark phase one of Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza. Instead, Israel is using the line to expand its control.
Along the Yellow Line, Israel has placed concrete yellow blocks, signaling areas Palestinians cannot approach. We have mapped the position of more than 100 yellow blocks. Most have been placed well beyond the agreed withdrawal line. Over time, Israel is moving these blocks further into the area where Palestinians are concentrated. With every expansion, the military destroys another neighborhood, preventing Palestinian return.
Israel also imposed an additional boundary, which it called the Orange Line. In some places, this line encroaches more than one kilometer beyond the Yellow Line.
At the same time, Israel has entrenched its military presence. Around every 1.8 kilometers along the Yellow Line, it has built a fortified military base. We have documented 34 active bases. Many bases, like this one in Bani Suheila, have been constructed on the ruins of Palestinian homes.
Israel has also demolished and compacted nearby buildings which remained standing. Building by building, Gaza’s landscape is being permanently reconfigured. This picture shows the neighborhood before it was erased.
AMY GOODMAN: On Tuesday, the U.N. special rapporteur on the Occupied Palestinian Territories, Francesca Albanese, called on the ICC, the International Criminal Court, to investigate incitement to genocide by government officials and media figures in Israel.

Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.
In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.
Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

I actually discovered about the Nimbus contract, which is the deal that Google has with the Israeli government and the IDF, a deal that includes cloud and AI services for — used by the military for war. I discovered about this deal when Google fired employees in the U.S. protesting over the deal in 2024. And at the beginning, in London, there was no internal movement. No Tech for Apartheid was at the time mainly a U.S. movement. And so, I felt really powerless. I just bought a Palestine hoodie. I went to the office with it, but I really didn’t know what to do. Then I went on maternity leave. And during maternity leave, I was watching the news every day, watching a live-streamed genocide, and I knew that my company was complicit. So, my first thought was resigning straightaway, not even coming back from maternity leave. But what changed my mind was that as the time to come back was coming, I met a colleague. We get analysis of the Israeli elections, the upcoming U.S. midterms, the pro-Palestine movement and more from Palestinian American scholar Rashid Khalidi and Pakistani British writer Tariq Ali. They are co-authors of the new book The Neck and the Sword: Palestine’s Unfinished Struggle. The book, an extended conversation between Khalidi and Ali over two years, offers an overview of Palestinian intellectual and political history, drawing its title from a famous phrase used by the renowned Palestinian writer Ghassan Kanafani to describe the futility of “peace talks” between occupier and occupied, saying it was akin to a “conversation between the sword and the neck.”
Kanafani was assassinated by Israel in 1972, “murdered simply because his words were too dangerous for Israel to tolerate,” says Khalidi.
Public opinion about Israel has grown increasingly negative in the United States and across much of the world in the wake of the genocide in Gaza, and it’s “not going to shift back,” says Khalidi. “People have seen something that cannot be unseen. They’ve seen genocide. They’ve seen slaughter. And Israel has no defense.”
“Even in countries with no history of a Palestine solidarity movement, suddenly the Palestine flag emerges,” says Ali. “Why? Because their governments are trying to stop dissent on this issue, so they are defying their governments.”

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a record fourth term in office, defeating far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro by 4 million votes in a runoff election on Sunday. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who remains under house arrest for plotting a coup against Lula four years ago. The younger Bolsonaro, who narrowly defeated Lula in the first round of voting earlier this month, is now refusing to concede.
Lula’s surprise comeback comes after weeks of student-led organizing and campaigning on his behalf, and amid accusations that U.S.-based tech companies were suppressing Lula’s reach online in favor of his Trump-aligned opponent. “The amount of organizing, the amount of marches and rallies, campaigning, pamphlets that we’ve seen the last three weeks has been something that I have never seen in my entire life, ever, covering elections for decades in so many different countries. It is absolutely unprecedented,” says Brazil-based journalist Michael Fox. “It is an absolute game-changer for the region.”
